subject: former child actors
one_liner: Dating for people who peaked before their adult teeth came in.
brand_voice_notes: A talent agency that pivoted into dating and never updated the paperwork. Speaks in casting-office shorthand: callbacks, sides, holding, wrap. Treats every user as a client with a filmography and every date as an audition. Never mentions the actual shows by real names. Never admits the careers are over; they are 'between seasons.'

hero.h1: Date someone who also peaked at nine.
hero.sub: Callback matches former child actors with other former child actors, so nobody has to explain the residuals, the lunchbox, or why they won't say the line.

features.title: Verified filmography
features.blurb: Every profile is checked against TV Guide archives, two fan wikis and a retired casting director named Phyllis. If your credit was cut in syndication, Phyllis will know, and she will say so.

features.title: Catchphrase compatibility
features.blurb: Our model scores how often each of you gets asked to say your line in public. Couples within 3 points report 41% fewer incidents at airport gates.

features.title: Recognition shield
features.blurb: First dates are booked at venues where the median diner is 22 and has never had basic cable. We call these rooms the blind spot. Phyllis scouts them personally.

demo_screen_concept: A swipe stack of 8x10 glossy headshot cards, each with a stapled mini-résumé: stage name, credits list with fake sitcoms and years, a 'still receiving residuals' badge, a Catchphrase Compatibility score out of 10, and a Recognition Risk meter. Controls are Pass, Callback (like), and 'Have my people call your people' (super-like). Chips filter by era (80s / 90s / 00s). A match triggers a 'You got the callback' modal with a fake call sheet for the first date: venue, call time, wardrobe notes. A side panel lists the day's callbacks.

design_direction.style: Casting-office headshot composite, studio-seamless daylight mode. The page is staged as a talent agency's submission wall: 8x10 glossy prints with a white border and a printed name strip along the bottom edge, résumés stapled to their backs, an illuminated APPLAUSE sign above the stage, and SMPTE broadcast color bars as the only divider. One light mode only. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: pegboard, cork, push pins, tape strips, aisle signs, shelf tags, pulp cells, grade stamps, vent holes, vinyl bladders, weld seams, chenille, brass plates, holographic foil, acrylic slabs, enamel plaques, terrazzo, bolts, rivets, hazard chevrons. Also absent: glassmorphism, blur, neon, dark mode, gradients behind body text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The 8x10 glossy: every card, tier and quote is a white print #FFFFFF with a 14px white border, a 1px #D8D3C9 edge, 2px radius, a subtle top-left sheen line, and a black name strip along the bottom in Abril Fatface. (2) The staple: a 22x6px silver bar (#B9BCC0 with a 1px #7D8186 underline), set at -8deg on the top-left of résumé panels only. (3) The applause sign: primary CTA and highlighted tier are a lit red box #C8102E with cream #FFF4D6 letters, a 2px inner cream keyline, square corners, and an on/off blink on hover. (4) The color bars: section dividers are 10px strips of seven SMPTE bars in desaturated tones. Headings are Abril Fatface, sentence case, tight. Body is Libre Franklin 17px/1.62. Every figure, year and score is IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures. Ground is a light studio-seamless grey #ECE9E3.

fonts.body: 'Libre Franklin', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: App Store style landing (hero with device-free headshot composite, features, reviews, pricing, download-style CTA)
design_direction.motion_vocab: Prints settle in from rotate(-1.5deg) translateY(10px) to rest; applause sign blinks off and on once on hover; headshot cards fling off-canvas with a rotation on swipe; all 200ms ease-out, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left: giant Abril Fatface headline with the applause-sign CTA below. Right: a fanned stack of three 8x10 glossies at slight rotations, one with a stapled résumé peeking out. Color bars under the hero.

images.rationale: photo-shaped demo (headshot swipe stack) gets 3 portrait cards, which the landing hero reuses as its fanned 8x10 composite, so no separate 16:9 hero was generated; the 4th image is a testimonial headshot for Dana Voss. The other two testimonials keep the CSS initials treatment.
